confirmed_ordinary_findings: Public archive segment creation previously lacked parent-directory durability before SQLite descriptor publication; the writer now stages, fsyncs, publishes with POSIX directory fsync (or Windows write-through rename), and publishes descriptors afterward. Singleton, batch, rollover, injected publication failure, and retry tests pass.
Batch archive state now advances immediately after durable bytes are appended and before chronology sampling; a raising clock callback no longer leaves the same writer permanently offset-stale.

The dual-public queue reconciliation integration now passes 100ms/500ms/1s injected lookup stalls with 3 measured service intervals per case. Measured maximum post-service gaps were 124ms, 519ms, and 1.023s against stall-inclusive bounds of 301ms, 701ms, and 1.201s. This is a small two-instrument integration, not broad-universe capacity qualification.
Bulk reference order had repeated compressed-block decoding beyond cache capacity; grouped lookup and ordered hydration remain separately focused and do not establish full mixed-workload scale.
Shared chronology DAG repeated dependencies exponentially; per-call proof caching has focused evidence but does not qualify the final integrated SHA.
